hints: Think separately about bonds within one polymer chain versus forces between different chains.
PVC is made from $\text{CH}_2\text{CHCl}$ units, so each single strand is already held together by strong C-C covalent bonds.
Check if PVC has ions, or O-H or N-H groups for hydrogen bonding, and if not, decide what weak intermolecular force must be left to attract one neutral chain to another.
walkthrough:
**Look Inside One Strand**

Think of one PVC chain as a long backbone of carbon atoms. Those atoms are joined by strong covalent bonds formed during addition polymerisation.

Repeat unit idea:
$$n\text{CH}_2=\text{CHCl} \rightarrow \text{-[CH}_2\text{-CHCl]}_n\text{-}$$

**Look Between Different Strands**

The question asks what holds separate strands to each other, not what holds atoms together inside one strand. That must be an intermolecular force, not a full chemical bond.

**Rule Out Strong Options**

PVC chains are neutral molecules, so there are no ionic bonds. PVC has C-H, C-C and C-Cl bonds only, so there is no O-H or N-H group and no lone pair on O or N to make hydrogen bonds. The only attraction left between the polar C-Cl groups and neighbouring chains is permanent dipole and induced dipole attractions, which are van der Waals forces.

options.A: Covalent bonds hold atoms together within one PVC chain, such as C-C and C-Cl, but they do not link one separate chain to another. Choosing this confuses intramolecular bonding with intermolecular forces.
options.B: Hydrogen bonds need H attached to N, O or F plus a lone pair on N, O or F. PVC contains only C, H and Cl, so it cannot form hydrogen bonds between chains.
options.C: Ionic bonds need oppositely charged ions with electron transfer. PVC is a neutral covalent polymer with no ions present, so ionic bonding is impossible here.
options.D: Separate neutral PVC strands are attracted by van der Waals forces, including dipole-dipole forces from the polar C-Cl bonds and London dispersion forces. These many weak attractions add up along the long chains to hold the solid together.
